Dear Editors of The R Journal,

We submit the article *seqbench: Anytime-Valid Sequential Benchmarking of Algorithms in R* for consideration as a contributed research article.

The article presents `seqbench`, an R package that turns the comparison of two algorithms on a benchmark into a pre-registered sequential experiment. Benchmarks in optimisation, machine learning and computational statistics are run and inspected sequentially, with adaptive budgets and early stopping, and fixed-sample tests lose their guarantees under that use. The package maintains a confidence sequence for the mean paired difference of losses that stays valid under optional stopping, adds a pre-registered margin of practical equivalence with a three-way decision rule that inherits the error control, accounts for cost and treats inconclusive outcomes as first-class results, and reports a full contract of what was assumed and consumed.

We believe the article fits The R Journal for three reasons. First, the package addresses a recurrent statistical failure in computational research with a tidyverse-native, tested and documented implementation; no package on CRAN offers this protocol. Second, the article contains a simulation study with 2,000 replications per cell, frozen before results were available, that measures the validity and cost of the package's boundaries against fixed-sample tests, an invalid repeatedly inspected test and the anytime-valid Gaussian confidence sequence of `safestats`. Third, we report the cost of distribution-free validity honestly: the Gaussian sequence with a known variance needs substantially fewer instances, and the article explains the mechanism and what a user can do about it.

Version 0.1.0 of the package is available from CRAN (https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=seqbench), and its documentation is at https://castlaboratory.github.io/seqbench/. The package has unit tests that check output values, documented examples for every user-facing function, a vignette with the full workflow and continuous integration on macOS, Windows and Linux. All experiment configurations, runner and analysis scripts are in the `experiments/` directory of the package repository (`castlaboratory/seqbench`, outside the package sources), the article source is in `paper/rjournal/` of the same repository, every table in the article is produced from archived results, and the data and scripts that rebuild the tables are included with this submission.

Sincerely,

André Leite, Raydonal Ospina and Cristiano Ferraz
CAST Lab, Universidade Federal de Pernambuco, and Universidade Federal da Bahia
